question: Should current CI targets require `deadcode:exports` while historical targets retain the compatibility fallback implemented by this PR?
rationale: The merged history contains two deliberate but competing CI policies: enforced export ratcheting and frozen-target compatibility, so the permanent contract needs explicit owner confirmation.

options.title: Enforce current, preserve historical
options.body: Narrow the Knip exclusions, require `deadcode:exports` on current targets, and retain the script-detection fallback for historical targets.

options.title: Keep exports advisory
options.body: Retain the current advisory policy for all targets and use the export scan only as a maintenance command.

options.title: Pause policy change
options.body: Leave the PR open until release-validation owners define a different versioned capability contract for frozen targets.

recommendation.title: Enforce current, preserve historical
recommendation.body: Narrow the Knip exclusions, require `deadcode:exports` on current targets, and retain the script-detection fallback for historical targets.

likelyOwner.reason: Authored the most recent merged change defining frozen-target dead-code compatibility and is best positioned to confirm that the proposed fallback preserves that contract.
